meta.title: Chevir - Translation System
meta.description: Chevir translation system - converts Azerbaijani Sign Language fingerspelling from camera to text, and text to avatar signing. Everything runs in the browser.
header.pageSubtitle: Azerbaijani Sign Language fingerspelling · everything runs in the browser
s2t.stage.cameraSub: detection runs on the raw frame
s2t.hint.lettersHold: Hold each letter for ~1 second: keep your hand still for static letters, sign the dynamic letters (ç, d, g, k, ö, ü, y, z) normally. To repeat the same letter, move your hand out of the pose first.
s2t.hint.lettersKeyboard: No camera? Test the decoder by typing letters from your keyboard:
s2t.hint.wordsRest: Hands rest at your sides. Sign one or more words, then lower your hands: the model looks at the whole sign and splits it into words. Your body and hands must be visible in frame.
s2t.hint.wordsF1Prefix: The model has been tested on people not seen in AzSLD (macro-F1
s2t.hint.wordsF1Suffix: ), but it's still experimental on live camera. Video never leaves your device.
s2t.hint.sentenceContinuous: Sign the sentence continuously: each word is captured about 1 second after you show it, no need to lower your hands between words. Lower your hands when the sentence ends - a two-second pause closes the sentence.
s2t.hint.sentenceF1Prefix: The model has been tested on sentences from people not seen in AzSLD (word F1
s2t.hint.sentenceF1Suffix: ). It's weaker on new sentences not in AzSLD (F1 ~0.6, vs ~0.8 on words it recognizes). Still experimental on live camera. Video never leaves your device.

about.heading: Model and measurements
about.decoderBody: The top 3 letters from each prediction enter the beam. Candidates are weighted with a letter-bigram language model (from the lexicon: {words} unique words, {prefixes} prefixes). Finally a lexicon check: an exact match gets a bonus; otherwise the closest real words are suggested by edit distance.
about.whyBrowserHeading: Why everything runs in the browser
about.whyBrowserBody: There is no server: video never leaves the device, latency is minimal, and the system can be hosted anywhere as a static file. Privacy isn't an incidental choice for an accessibility product - sign language video carries the user's face and identity.
about.nonLetters.intro: The system runs the fingerspelling model (fingerspelling_33.h5) as-is. Keras weights are exported as raw float32; the forward pass is computed in JS with 4 matmuls - no TensorFlow.js needed. The port was verified against a numpy reference, max difference 4.8e-7 (the float32 limit).
about.nonLetters.featuresValue: MediaPipe Hands, first hand, raw x/y/z
about.nonLetters.whenWrittenBody: A letter is only typed from the camera when the hand is steady: the hand must be visible in every frame of a 20-frame window, the motion measure must stay low (steady pose 0.00-0.04, transition 0.06-0.11), the model must be at least 45% confident, and the same letter must be confirmed in 3 consecutive predictions. Without these conditions, the moment a hand enters the frame - mixed with empty frames - used to read as a dynamic letter: for example 5 empty frames + 15 frames of “s” means ö (0.89) to the model.
about.azsldIntro: {images} images (AzSLD Fingerspelling, Zenodo 14222948), hand detected in {detectRate}% of them.
about.azsldNote1: (1) The near-zero score on dynamic letters isn't a model failure, it's an artifact of the measurement method: a single frame is repeated 20 times, and motion simply can't be represented that way. Given as a real sequence, ç and ö are recognized correctly.
about.azsldNote2: (2) These images may be part of the model's training data - meaning the numbers are optimistic, not a held-out test set.
about.letters.intro: The fingerspelling model reads hand shape (scale-invariant, independent of camera distance and hand position in frame) and motion from MediaPipe hand landmarks, looking at the last {window} frames ({seconds}s at 30fps). Body and face are not used. It recognizes all 32 letters, including the dynamic ones ({dynamicList}), and can say “no letter” ({noneLabel}).
about.letters.trainingValue: AzSLD: letters in sentences (two cameras), Fingerspelling photos and clips
about.letters.testHeading: Test: people unseen by the model
about.letters.sources.sentence: Letters in AzSLD sentences, front camera
about.letters.testNote: The old model (raw hand coordinates from 20 frames, 4-layer network) was measured on the same test samples. It may have seen the Fingerspelling photos during training - its result on that row is optimistic.
about.letters.whenWrittenBody: The model predicts every {stride} frames. A letter is typed once the hand is visible in every frame of the window, the model is at least {confidence}% confident, and the same letter is confirmed in {dwell} consecutive predictions. Static letters require a steady hand; dynamic letters don't have this requirement. To repeat the same letter, move your hand out of the pose or show a different letter first.
